PARENT_NARROWING_DECLARATION.why_this_section_exists: The binding HPO is STRICTER than the parent authority at exactly one point. Stating that explicitly is required; discovering it during audit is not acceptable.
PARENT_NARROWING_DECLARATION.parent_text: MULTI_ORG_TENANT_SCOPE_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0 SESSION_SCOPE.no_selection_behavior.single_membership_case: 'Where the subject has exactly one selectable membership, the application MAY present that organization as the selection, but it MUST do so by making an explicit selection (writing the carrier), not by inferring a scope at request time.'
PARENT_NARROWING_DECLARATION.hpo_text: NO_AUTO_SELECTION = BINDING. Candidates >= 1, INCLUDING candidates = 1, routes to the selector. No carrier write during routing.
PARENT_NARROWING_DECLARATION.relationship: NARROWING, NOT CONFLICT. The parent grants a discretionary MAY; the HPO declines to exercise it. Declining a permission is always available to a subordinate authority. The parent's MUST (that any selection be an explicit carrier write, never a request-time inference) is preserved intact and is in fact strengthened: under this artifact the carrier is written ONLY by the pre-existing governed selection act at app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/actions.ts, never by a routing decision.
PARENT_NARROWING_DECLARATION.fail_closed_check: If a future adjudication reads this as a CONFLICT rather than a NARROWING, the correct disposition is STOP AND ESCALATE, not silent reconciliation in either direction. It is recorded here so that the question is answerable from the artifact.
PARENT_NARROWING_DECLARATION.what_would_have_been_a_real_conflict: An HPO instruction to auto-select for candidates = 1 WITHOUT writing the carrier. That would violate the parent's MUST and its 'why' clause ('Inference at request time is exactly SI-2, re-created under a new name'). No such instruction was given.

DEFECT.classification: ROUTING DEFECT. NOT a schema defect, NOT a privilege defect, NOT an S3 semantics defect.
DEFECT.one_sentence: S3 gave the request principal a two-valued refusal discriminator, but every routing consumer still asks the pre-S3 boolean question 'is membership null', which is TRUE under both values — so a returning member who simply has no selected-organization carrier is routed to organization CREATION instead of organization SELECTION.

emission_sites: RETURN SITE 1 — lib/auth/database-context.ts:448. Carrier absent (or malformed). Code = TENANCY_NO_ORGANIZATION_SELECTED. membership = null. pendingRevalidationRefusal = null.

RETURN SITE 2 — lib/auth/database-context.ts:472. Carrier names an organization with no active membership for this subject. Code = TENANCY_SELECTED_ORGANIZATION_NOT_A_MEMBER. membership = null. pendingRevalidationRefusal = the attempted organization id.

RETURN SITE 3 — lib/auth/database-context.ts:511. Membership EXISTS and is returned; only the organization ROW could not be read. Code = TENANCY_SELECTED_ORGANIZATION_NOT_A_MEMBER as a REUSED CARRIER. membership = NON-NULL. pendingRevalidationRefusal = null.

ROUTING_CONTRACT.applies_to: An AUTHENTICATED subject. An unauthenticated subject is out of scope and its existing redirect to /login is preserved verbatim at every site.
ROUTING_CONTRACT.evaluation_order_is_normative: The four rules below are ORDERED. An implementation that evaluates them in a different order can produce a different destination for the same principal, so the order is part of the contract, not a presentation choice.

R1_SUPER_ADMIN_PRESERVED_VERBATIM.rule: Where the existing super-admin contract applies, it is preserved VERBATIM and is evaluated BEFORE any selector question.
R1_SUPER_ADMIN_PRESERVED_VERBATIM.concrete: lib/auth/session.ts:179 — if (principal.user.isSuperAdmin) redirect('/admin') — keeps its position ahead of the /app/onboarding branch and keeps its destination.
R1_SUPER_ADMIN_PRESERVED_VERBATIM.prohibition: A super-admin without a membership MUST NOT be routed to /app/organizations/select. SUPERADMIN_BOUNDARY.what_superadmins_retain is explicit that superadmins reach tenant data 'through a different, explicit door'; sending them to the tenant selector would be that door reopened by accident.

R2_NO_CARRIER.action: Call the EXISTING selectable-membership enumerator: listSelectableMemberships(), exported from lib/auth/session.ts:83 as a re-export of lib/auth/database-context.ts:661.
R2_NO_CARRIER.branch_one_or_more: candidates.length >= 1 -> route to /app/organizations/select. THIS INCLUDES candidates.length === 1.

R3_STALE_OR_NON_MEMBER_CARRIER.action: Clear the stale carrier, THEN route to /app/organizations/select carrying the governed refusal/error semantics already implemented for that route.
R3_STALE_OR_NON_MEMBER_CARRIER.ordering_is_normative: The carrier is cleared BEFORE the redirect is issued. If the redirect were issued first, the next request would re-enter R3 with the same stale carrier and the graph would not terminate.
R3_STALE_OR_NON_MEMBER_CARRIER.error_semantics_reuse: The selector route already renders a governed explanation for this exact condition under the existing key not_a_member (app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/page.tsx:42 — 'No perteneces a esa organización, o tu membresía ya no está activa.'), reached today via app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/actions.ts:116. This contract REUSES that key and MUST NOT invent a new error vocabulary.
R3_STALE_OR_NON_MEMBER_CARRIER.fallback_prohibition: Never fall back to another membership, not even when the subject holds exactly one other active membership. This is SECOND_ORG_MEMBERSHIP B4, whose B4_classification names it 'the failure mode most likely to be introduced as a UX nicety'. Routing the subject to the selector is not a fallback: the subject chooses, the application does not choose for them.

R4_THIRD_RETURN_SITE_IS_NOT_A_SELECTOR_C.derivation: DERIVED BY THIS MISSION FROM MEASURED CODE. It was not supplied by the HPO and it corrects a latent hazard in a contract keyed on the refusal code alone.
R4_THIRD_RETURN_SITE_IS_NOT_A_SELECTOR_C.precondition: principal.membership !== null AND principal.organizationRefusalCode === 'TENANCY_SELECTED_ORGANIZATION_NOT_A_MEMBER' (lib/auth/database-context.ts:511, RETURN SITE 3).
R4_THIRD_RETURN_SITE_IS_NOT_A_SELECTOR_C.the_hazard: At this site the code is a REUSED CARRIER for an unreadable ORGANISATION ROW, and the membership DEMONSTRABLY EXISTS — it was loaded, is non-null, and is returned in the same object. A routing rule keyed on the CODE ALONE would treat this subject as holding a stale carrier, CLEAR a perfectly valid carrier, and evict a genuine member from their chosen scope on a transient organisation-read failure.
R4_THIRD_RETURN_SITE_IS_NOT_A_SELECTOR_C.why_this_is_a_carried_constraint_not_an_: The repository already defends its AUDIT emitter against exactly this trap and says so in terms: lib/auth/database-context.ts:415-418 states that pendingRevalidationRefusal 'is deliberately NOT derived from organizationRefusalCode: that code is returned at TWO structurally different sites below and is TRUE at only one of them', and :495-:501 states that 'An emitter keyed on organizationRefusalCode would therefore write a FALSE audit row here'. This rule transposes that same discipline from the AUDIT dimension to the ROUTING dimension, where it had not yet been stated.
R4_THIRD_RETURN_SITE_IS_NOT_A_SELECTOR_C.rule: Every routing predicate in this contract is a CONJUNCTION of the refusal code AND membership === null. The code alone is NEVER sufficient to route. RETURN SITE 3 is therefore matched by NEITHER R2 NOR R3.
R4_THIRD_RETURN_SITE_IS_NOT_A_SELECTOR_C.disposition_of_site_3: EXCLUDED FROM THIS NODE, NOT ABSORBED. It remains the pre-existing open governed question TENANCY_ORGANIZATION_READABILITY_INVARIANT_SUCCESSOR_REQUIRED (recorded at MULTI_ORG_S1_S2_EXECUTION_SCOPE_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_v1.0.6.json:320 and :723, ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.25.json:265 and :805, owner TO_BE_MAPPED, BLOCKS_THIS_NODE false). This artifact allocates it no verb, no destination and no carrier mutation. Its existing behaviour — the requireOrganizationAccess membership-AND-organization conjunction at lib/auth/session.ts:177 — is preserved unchanged, which keeps it fail-closed.

R5_TERMINATION.rule: The routing graph must terminate. No destination of this contract may itself re-enter the contract with the same principal state.
R5_TERMINATION.measured_basis: app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/page.tsx calls only requireAuth() at :50 and renders; with candidates.length === 0 it renders an explanation at :88 rather than redirecting. The selector is TERMINAL — it has no outbound redirect on any candidate count — so no cycle through it is constructible. /app/onboarding is likewise served from app/(authenticated)/, whose layout calls only requireAuth() (app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx:76), and is therefore outside the organisation gate that would otherwise redirect back to it.

NO_CARRIER_WRITE_DURING_ROUTING.rule: No rule of this contract writes the selected-organization carrier. R3 CLEARS a carrier; clearing is not selecting, and it leaves the subject with no scope rather than with a scope they did not choose.
NO_CARRIER_WRITE_DURING_ROUTING.sole_permitted_writer_unchanged: The carrier is written only by the pre-existing governed selection act at app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/actions.ts, which independently revalidates candidacy at :101-:103 before writing.

NO_AUTO_SELECTION.rule: For candidates.length === 1 the destination is the SELECTOR, identically to candidates.length >= 2. The single-candidate case gets no shortcut.
prohibited_selection_strategies: automatic selection of the sole candidate
pick-first / .limit(1) over an unqualified user predicate
any inference of scope from whatever memberships happen to exist
any carrier write performed by a routing decision rather than by the governed selection act
NO_AUTO_SELECTION.why_the_single_candidate_case_is_the_loa: It is the only case where auto-selection is invisible in ordinary use — with one membership the user cannot tell an automatic choice from their own. It is therefore the case that will be introduced as a convenience and never noticed. SESSION_SCOPE.no_selection_behavior.why names the consequence exactly: 'Inference at request time is exactly SI-2, re-created under a new name.'
NO_AUTO_SELECTION.observability_of_compliance: The parent supplies the discriminating observation directly: SESSION_SCOPE.no_selection_behavior.single_membership_case — 'The distinction is observable: after the selection the carrier exists; under inference it never would.' N-A1-1 asserts precisely that, on the single-candidate route.
NO_AUTO_SELECTION.relationship_to_parent: See PARENT_NARROWING_DECLARATION. This is the parent's discretionary MAY declined, not the parent's MUST contradicted.

AUDIT_SEMANTICS.frozen: THIS NODE ADDS NO AUDIT EVENT AND REMOVES NONE.

no_new_event_for_absent_carrier.rule: Routing a subject away from an absent selected-organization carrier (R2) MUST NOT emit an audit event, on either branch — neither the 0-candidate route to onboarding nor the >=1-candidate route to the selector.
no_new_event_for_absent_carrier.carried_rationale: The site-1 rationale is already frozen in the implementation and is carried, not re-derived: lib/auth/database-context.ts:433-:446 — 'RETURN SITE 1 — AND IT AUDITS NOTHING, WHICH IS THE POINT... reaching this line does not mean anyone ATTEMPTED anything. In the overwhelmingly common case it is an ordinary signed-in user who has not selected yet — onboarding, not refusal. An audit row here would record a refusal of an attempt that never happened, on almost every request such a user makes.'
no_new_event_for_absent_carrier.why_routing_does_not_change_it: Routing is an observation of the absence, not an attempt. Making the absence REACHABLE by a new destination does not convert it into an attempt. If anything the argument strengthens: after this repair the no-carrier state is the ORDINARY state of every returning member at the start of every session, so an event here would be pure volume with no refusal behind it.

existing_site_2_refusal_preserved.rule: The membership-revalidation refusal audit at RETURN SITE 2 is PRESERVED EXACTLY: same verb, same subject, same emission site, same split between the deciding transaction and the write.
existing_site_2_refusal_preserved.mechanism_preserved: lib/auth/database-context.ts:471-:474 returns pendingRevalidationRefusal rather than writing it, and :597-:606 discharges the obligation through a SEPARATE withDatabaseIdentityContext that calls emitMembershipRevalidationRefused. The architectural reason is frozen at :400-:406: writing the audit row inside the deciding transaction 'would couple the observation to the decision: a failing INSERT would roll the whole transaction back, so the audit surface could change what the authorization surface answers' (HPO ADJUDICATION D).
existing_site_2_refusal_preserved.borrowed_transaction_branch_also_preserv: There is a SECOND discharge path at lib/auth/database-context.ts:554-:570: when the deciding transaction was BORROWED from a caller, the audit cannot be isolated, and the implementation refuses LOUDLY (throws) rather than writing the row into the caller's transaction or silently skipping it — 'Both remaining options are failures; this picks the LOUD one.' Routing must not convert that loud failure into a redirect. A subject whose principal resolution throws here is not a subject with no carrier, and must not be routed as if they were.
existing_site_2_refusal_preserved.consequence_for_R3: R3 routes AFTER the principal has already been resolved, so the refusal is recorded by the existing mechanism before routing runs. R3 must not re-emit it, must not suppress it, and must not move it.

no_emitter_may_be_keyed_on_the_code.rule: No audit emitter added or modified by this node may key on organizationRefusalCode. This node adds none, so the rule is satisfied vacuously — it is stated so that the vacuity is deliberate and auditable rather than accidental.
no_emitter_may_be_keyed_on_the_code.reason: lib/auth/database-context.ts:495-:501 — an emitter keyed on the code writes a FALSE row at RETURN SITE 3, asserting an absent membership that the same return value disproves.

AUDIT_SEMANTICS.no_tenant_content: AUDIT_VERBS.prohibited is carried unchanged: no audit verb may record the CONTENT of tenant data. Attribution and outcome only. This node records nothing at all, so it cannot violate it.

MECHANICALLY_FORCED_EXISTING_TEST_EDITS.classification: MECHANICAL TEST CORRECTION, NOT AUTHORITY WEAKENING.
MECHANICALLY_FORCED_EXISTING_TEST_EDITS.why_that_classification_is_defensible: Every assertion these suites make today is TRUE of the pre-repair system and remains a property somebody wants. What changes is that a single fixture is no longer EXPRESSIVE ENOUGH: it names a principal state ('member-less') that the repair splits into two states with two different correct destinations. The edits ADD the missing operand and RE-PIN each existing assertion to the operand it was always about. No assertion is deleted, no expectation is loosened, and no destination that is correct today becomes unasserted. If any edit removes a control instead of re-pinning it, this classification fails and the mission STOPS.

It sets NO organizationRefusalCode at all and stubs NO enumerator, so once routing reads either one, this single fixture cannot distinguish genuine memberless/founding from member-with-no-carrier. It is the direct fixture-level image of the production defect.
